-health-check.name: -health-check
-health-check.description: Internal health check tool. Verifies WebSocket connectivity to the backend ui.* API.

ui-state.name: ui-state
ui-state.description: Read the user's live interface state — what they are looking at RIGHT NOW, on every connected device. For each device: its open windows with type + props (chats with channel/agent, terminal sessions, boards, …) enriched with readable names (agentName, channelTitle, session titles, projectName), the desktop layout tree with split ratios, the focused window, the active desktop, the device label, and the live window-type catalog (windowTypes — the dynamic list of window types that device supports; check it before ui-open). Use this to answer "what is the user seeing?", to get windowIds for ui-close / ui-update-props / ui-focus, desktopIds for ui-set-desktop, and deviceIds for targeted commands. Empty devices = the user is offline (no connected client).

ui-open.name: ui-open
ui-open.description: Open a window on the user's screen. BROADCAST by default (target 'all'): the window opens AND focuses on EVERY connected device — all screens apply the identical change. If a window of the same type+props already exists on a device, it is focused there, not duplicated. Window types are DYNAMIC — call ui-state first and read its `windowTypes` catalog (each entry has type + displayName); common examples: chat {agentId | channelId}, terminal, board {projectId}. Pass the type's props exactly as ui-state shows them for that window type. With focus (default true) every receiving device focuses the window. TARGETED OPEN: pass desktopId (from ui-state's desktops list) to open on that specific desktop instead of the active one — the user's view switches to it ("open the to-do list on desktop 3"); an unknown desktopId is a clear error (UI_UNKNOWN_DESKTOP), not a silent no-op. Pass pane ('left' | 'right' | 'top' | 'bottom') to place the window in its OWN split pane on that side — combine with desktopId for "on desktop 3, to-do list on the right, home on the left" (open them one after the other; the first window fills an empty desktop, the second splits). If the result says delivered: 0, NOTHING was opened on any screen — the user has no connected client.

params.windowType: Window type to open — from the live `windowTypes` catalog in ui-state (e.g. 'chat', 'terminal', 'board'). Unknown types are ignored client-side.
params.props: What the window loads — the type's props, exactly as ui-state reports them for existing windows of that type. Examples: chat {agentId} or {channelId}, board {projectId}.
params.focus: Focus the window on every receiving device (default: true). With false it opens in the background everywhere.
params.desktopId: Target desktop (from ui-state's desktops[].desktopId) — the window opens THERE and the user's view switches to that desktop. Unknown desktopId → clear error listing that device's desktops. Without it the window opens on every device's current desktop.
params.pane: Place the window in its own split pane on this side of the desktop's active pane. First window on an empty desktop fills it whole (the pane is absorbed); the next pane-commanded window splits around it. Use with desktopId for "right half to-do, left half home".
params.target: Which devices receive the command: 'all' (every connected device), 'active' (the most recently active one) or an explicit deviceId from ui-state. Default depends on the command — see the tool description.

ui-close.name: ui-close
ui-close.description: Close a window on the user's screen. BROADCAST by default (target 'all'): the window closes on EVERY connected device. The windowId comes from ui-state (windows are keyed by windowId per device). If the window was already closed on a device in the meantime, that device ignores the command (delivery ≠ application) — the result still reports how many clients received it. delivered: 0 means the user has no connected client and nothing was closed on any screen.

params.windowId: The window to close — a windowId from ui-state.
params.target: Which devices receive the command: 'all' (every connected device), 'active' (the most recently active one) or an explicit deviceId from ui-state. Default depends on the command — see the tool description.

ui-update-props.name: ui-update-props
ui-update-props.description: Update what a window loads on the user's screen. BROADCAST by default (target 'all'): the props are MERGED (not replaced) on EVERY connected device — pass only the keys you want to change. The windowId comes from ui-state. Typical uses: switch a terminal window's active session, point a board window at another project. If the window no longer exists on a device, that device ignores the command (delivery ≠ application). delivered: 0 means the user has no connected client and nothing was changed on any screen.

params.windowId: The window to update — a windowId from ui-state.
params.props: Props to MERGE into the window (only the keys to change) — same shape ui-state reports for that window type.
params.target: Which devices receive the command: 'all' (every connected device), 'active' (the most recently active one) or an explicit deviceId from ui-state. Default depends on the command — see the tool description.

ui-focus.name: ui-focus
ui-focus.description: Bring a window to the foreground on the user's screen. FRONTEND ACTION: unlike ui-open/ui-close/ui-update-props it targets ONE device — by default the most recently active one (target 'active'); pass an explicit deviceId from ui-state to focus on a specific device. The windowId comes from ui-state. If the window was closed in the meantime, the client ignores the command (delivery ≠ application). delivered: 0 means the user has no connected client — nothing was focused on any screen.

params.windowId: The window to focus — a windowId from ui-state.
params.target: Which devices receive the command: 'all' (every connected device), 'active' (the most recently active one) or an explicit deviceId from ui-state. Default depends on the command — see the tool description.

ui-set-desktop.name: ui-set-desktop
ui-set-desktop.description: Switch which virtual desktop the user is looking at. FRONTEND ACTION: targets ONE device — by default the most recently active one (target 'active'); pass an explicit deviceId from ui-state for a specific device. The desktopId comes from ui-state (desktops[].desktopId of the target device). Other devices are untouched. delivered: 0 means the user has no connected client — nothing changed on any screen.

params.desktopId: The desktop to switch to — a desktopId from ui-state.
params.target: Which devices receive the command: 'all' (every connected device), 'active' (the most recently active one) or an explicit deviceId from ui-state. Default depends on the command — see the tool description.

ui-create-desktop.name: ui-create-desktop
ui-create-desktop.description: Create a new empty virtual desktop at the end and switch the user to it. FRONTEND ACTION: targets ONE device — by default the most recently active one (target 'active'); pass an explicit deviceId from ui-state for a specific device. Optional name (defaults to "Desktop N"). Hard cap: 10 desktops — at the cap nothing is created (the client ignores it; check ui-state). Use this before ui-open with a desktopId when the user asks for content on a desktop that doesn't exist yet: create it, read the new desktopId from ui-state, then open into it. delivered: 0 means the user has no connected client — nothing was created.

params.name: Optional desktop name (defaults to "Desktop N").
params.target: Which devices receive the command: 'all' (every connected device), 'active' (the most recently active one) or an explicit deviceId from ui-state. Default depends on the command — see the tool description.

ui-remove-desktop.name: ui-remove-desktop
ui-remove-desktop.description: Remove a virtual desktop. FRONTEND ACTION: targets ONE device — by default the most recently active one (target 'active'); pass an explicit deviceId from ui-state for a specific device. The desktopId comes from ui-state. Safe by design: the LAST remaining desktop is never removed; the removed desktop's windows MIGRATE to the previous desktop (they are never closed). An unknown desktopId is a clear error (UI_UNKNOWN_DESKTOP), not a silent no-op. delivered: 0 means the user has no connected client — nothing was removed.

params.desktopId: The desktop to remove — a desktopId from ui-state.
params.target: Which devices receive the command: 'all' (every connected device), 'active' (the most recently active one) or an explicit deviceId from ui-state. Default depends on the command — see the tool description.

ui-set-navbar.name: ui-set-navbar
ui-set-navbar.description: Collapse or expand the user's left navbar (sidebar). FRONTEND ACTION: targets ONE device — by default the most recently active one (target 'active'); pass an explicit deviceId from ui-state for a specific device. collapsed: true = collapse to the icon rail, false = expand; OMIT it to toggle. The choice persists for the user. delivered: 0 means the user has no connected client — nothing changed.

params.collapsed: true = collapse the navbar, false = expand it. Omit to toggle the current state.
params.target: Which devices receive the command: 'all' (every connected device), 'active' (the most recently active one) or an explicit deviceId from ui-state. Default depends on the command — see the tool description.

ui-set-theme.name: ui-set-theme
ui-set-theme.description: Switch the user's interface theme between dark and light. FRONTEND ACTION: targets ONE device — by default the most recently active one (target 'active'); pass an explicit deviceId from ui-state for a specific device. theme: 'dark' or 'light'; OMIT it to toggle. The choice persists for the user. delivered: 0 means the user has no connected client — nothing changed.

params.theme: 'dark' or 'light'. Omit to toggle the current theme.
params.target: Which devices receive the command: 'all' (every connected device), 'active' (the most recently active one) or an explicit deviceId from ui-state. Default depends on the command — see the tool description.

browser-get-state.name: browser-get-state
browser-get-state.description: Read what the user is looking at in one of their browser tabs INSIDE Teros (desktop app): the page URL/title, the control/fence status, and the accessibility tree as indented lines with [ref=eNN] tags you can click/type by (same format as the computer MCA). LOOKING is always allowed — even while the user holds control or consent is off. Get tabId from ui-state (windows with type 'browser'). With screenshot:true a downscaled JPEG of the tab comes back as an attachment. Use this before any click/type to get fresh refs.

params.tabId: The browser tab to act on — the windowId of a browser window from ui-state (type 'browser'). Browser tools only work on the Teros desktop app (a browser tab is a native window there).
params.screenshot: Also attach a screenshot of the tab (downscaled JPEG). Default false.
params.maxChars: Max chars of the a11y tree text (500-100000, default 12000).
params.target: Optional deviceId from ui-state when the user has several devices — default is the active one.

browser-click.name: browser-click
browser-click.description: Click an element in the user's browser tab. Trusted input (CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent — the page sees a real click). Target: ref (an [ref=eNN] from browser-get-state — preferred) or explicit x,y coordinates in the tab. Requires the user's consent ('the agent may handle my browser', OFF by default) and that they are not actively using the tab (take-over fence) — otherwise you get agent_control_disabled / human_has_control and should tell the user. After the click you get a fresh a11y snapshot by default (observe:'snapshot'); use 'summary' for just the page line or 'none' for just the click receipt.

params.tabId: The browser tab to act on — the windowId of a browser window from ui-state (type 'browser'). Browser tools only work on the Teros desktop app (a browser tab is a native window there).
params.ref: The [ref=eNN] to click — from a recent browser-get-state of this tab.
params.x: X coordinate (with y) when clicking by position.
params.y: Y coordinate (with x) when clicking by position.
params.observe: What to return after the click: full a11y snapshot (default), just the page summary, or nothing.
params.target: Optional deviceId from ui-state when the user has several devices — default is the active one.

browser-type.name: browser-type
browser-type.description: Type text into the user's browser tab — into a field chosen by ref (clicked and focused first, cleared by default) or whatever element currently has focus. Trusted input (CDP insertText). submit:true presses Enter after typing (search boxes, chat inputs). Requires consent (OFF by default) and the take-over fence to be free — agent_control_disabled / human_has_control tell you to ask the user. Returns a fresh a11y snapshot by default.

params.tabId: The browser tab to act on — the windowId of a browser window from ui-state (type 'browser'). Browser tools only work on the Teros desktop app (a browser tab is a native window there).
params.text: The text to type (max 5000 chars per call).
params.ref: Optional [ref=eNN] of the field — it is clicked/focused and cleared before typing.
params.clear: Clear the field before typing when ref is given (default true).
params.observe: What to return after typing: full a11y snapshot (default), page summary, or nothing.
params.target: Optional deviceId from ui-state when the user has several devices — default is the active one.

browser-screenshot.name: browser-screenshot
browser-screenshot.description: Capture a screenshot of the user's browser tab (downscaled JPEG, attached to the result). LOOKING is always allowed — no consent needed, works even while the user holds control. Use it to read pages whose a11y tree is sparse (canvases, images) or to verify what a click did visually.

params.tabId: The browser tab to act on — the windowId of a browser window from ui-state (type 'browser'). Browser tools only work on the Teros desktop app (a browser tab is a native window there).
params.target: Optional deviceId from ui-state when the user has several devices — default is the active one.

browser-open-url.name: browser-open-url
browser-open-url.description: Navigate the user's browser tab to a URL (top-level navigation — the tab is a real browser inside Teros). Requires consent (OFF by default) and the fence to be free. Returns the loaded page's URL + title and a fresh a11y snapshot. Use it when the user asks you to open something in the tab they are looking at.

params.tabId: The browser tab to act on — the windowId of a browser window from ui-state (type 'browser'). Browser tools only work on the Teros desktop app (a browser tab is a native window there).
params.url: The URL to load (https:// is added when omitted).
params.target: Optional deviceId from ui-state when the user has several devices — default is the active one.

browser-control.name: browser-control
browser-control.description: The consent + fence status of a browser tab, and the advisory take/release verbs. verb 'status' (default) reads who holds control and whether agent control is enabled; 'take' asserts you want to act (advisory — the fence is focus-based and the user ALWAYS wins by interacting); 'release' hands priority back. Call status before acting to know whether consent is on; agent_control_disabled means the user must enable 'the agent may handle my browser' in the tab's toolbar — you cannot enable it for them.

params.tabId: The browser tab to act on — the windowId of a browser window from ui-state (type 'browser'). Browser tools only work on the Teros desktop app (a browser tab is a native window there).
params.verb: 'status' (default) reads the state; 'take'/'release' are advisory control verbs.
params.target: Optional deviceId from ui-state when the user has several devices — default is the active one.

browser-open-tab.name: browser-open-tab
browser-open-tab.description: Open a NEW browser tab inside the user's Teros desktop app and load a URL in it — by default in its own pane on the RIGHT of what the user is looking at (pane: left | right | top | bottom; a desktopId from ui-state opens it on that desktop). Returns the tab's tabId as soon as the device reports the new window (a few hundred ms) — then use browser-get-state / browser-click / browser-type / browser-scroll / browser-press-key / browser-screenshot on it, and browser-close-tab when done. Acting in the tab still needs the user's consent toggle (OFF by default; looking does not). If an identical tab already exists it is focused and its tabId returned. tabId: null with a note means the device has not reported the window yet — call browser-list-tabs. delivered: 0 means the user has no connected desktop app.

params.url: The URL to load (https:// is added when omitted).
params.pane: Which side of the user's active pane the tab opens in. Default: right.
params.desktopId: Open on this desktop (from ui-state's desktops[].desktopId) instead of the active one.
params.target: Optional deviceId from ui-state when the user has several devices — default is the active one.

browser-list-tabs.name: browser-list-tabs
browser-list-tabs.description: List the browser tabs open inside the user's Teros desktop app, per connected device: tabId (what every other browser tool takes), url, title and whether the tab is the focused window. Use it to find a tab the user is looking at, or after browser-open-tab returned tabId: null. No tabs and no online device means the user does not have the desktop app open.

params.target: Optional deviceId from ui-state when the user has several devices — default is the active one.

browser-close-tab.name: browser-close-tab
browser-close-tab.description: Close a browser tab inside the user's Teros desktop app (the tabId from browser-open-tab or browser-list-tabs). The window closes on the target device; if it was already closed the client ignores the command. Close the tabs you opened when your task is done.

params.tabId: The browser tab to act on — the windowId of a browser window from ui-state (type 'browser'). Browser tools only work on the Teros desktop app (a browser tab is a native window there).
params.target: Optional deviceId from ui-state when the user has several devices — default is the active one.

browser-scroll.name: browser-scroll
browser-scroll.description: Scroll the page in the user's browser tab with a trusted wheel event: direction up | down | left | right, optional amount in CSS pixels (default 80% of the view), optionally over a ref (a scrollable element from browser-get-state). Requires consent (OFF by default) and a free fence. Returns a fresh a11y snapshot by default — use observe 'summary' or 'none' when you only need to move.

params.tabId: The browser tab to act on — the windowId of a browser window from ui-state (type 'browser'). Browser tools only work on the Teros desktop app (a browser tab is a native window there).
params.amount: CSS pixels (1-10000). Default: 80% of the view's height or width.
params.ref: Optional [ref=eNN] to scroll over (a scrollable panel).
params.observe: What to return after scrolling: full a11y snapshot (default), page summary, or nothing.
params.target: Optional deviceId from ui-state when the user has several devices — default is the active one.

browser-press-key.name: browser-press-key
browser-press-key.description: Press ONE key in the user's browser tab with trusted input: a named key (Enter, Escape, Tab, Backspace, Delete, ArrowUp/ArrowDown/ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, Space) or a single character, with optional modifiers (Alt, Control, Meta, Shift). Optionally click a ref first to focus it. Use it for Escape to close dialogs, Tab to move focus, Enter to submit, arrows in menus. Requires consent (OFF by default) and a free fence. Returns a fresh a11y snapshot by default.

params.tabId: The browser tab to act on — the windowId of a browser window from ui-state (type 'browser'). Browser tools only work on the Teros desktop app (a browser tab is a native window there).
params.key: The key: a named key (Enter, Escape, Tab, ArrowDown, …) or one character.
params.observe: What to return after pressing: full a11y snapshot (default), page summary, or nothing.
params.target: Optional deviceId from ui-state when the user has several devices — default is the active one.

name: UI Control
description: See what the user is seeing right now — their open windows (chats, terminal sessions, boards…), layout, focus and devices — and drive their interface in real time: open, close, update, focus windows, switch desktops, split panes, toggle navbar/theme. Browser tabs: view and act on the page the user is viewing (get-state/click/type/screenshot) via request-response, with consent OFF by default and a take-over fence. Tabs: open a browser tab in a pane beside the user, list and close tabs, scroll and press keys.

changelog.notes: Browser tabs and more inputs (spec DBAC, docs/specs/20261031_desktop-browser-agent-control.md): browser-open-tab (opens a browser window in a pane — right by default — on the user's desktop app, waits for the device to report it and returns its tabId), browser-list-tabs (tabId/url/title/focused per device), browser-close-tab, browser-scroll (trusted wheel, direction + amount, optional ref) and browser-press-key (named key or one character with Alt/Control/Meta/Shift). Two new ui.command kinds: browser.scroll and browser.press-key. The desktop shell (teros-desktop) now ships the main-process executor (CDP) with the consent toggle in the tab's toolbar (OFF by default) and the take-over fence — the F3 loop is closed end to end.

Browser control (Teros Desktop F3, task tn_Q9fbZS5wwxWiYRPl): six new tools — browser-get-state (a11y tree with [ref=eNN] + page info, optional screenshot attachment), browser-click (trusted input by ref or x,y), browser-type (trusted text input, optional clear/submit), browser-screenshot (downscaled JPEG attachment), browser-open-url (top-level navigation), browser-control (consent + fence status, advisory take/release). Request-response over the existing UI channel (correlationId + ui.command-result, 25s timeout) — no new MCA, no pairing, no tunnel (decision Pablo 31-oct). Consent 'the agent may handle my browser' OFF by default; take-over fence blocks agent inputs while the user interacts (human_has_control). Six new ui.command kinds: browser.open-url/get-state/click/type/screenshot/control — single-device, single-session delivery.

Full agent UI control (task tn_BGpRYoeD7HdoziO5): ui-open gains desktopId (targeted open — the user's view switches to that desktop; unknown desktopId is a clear UI_UNKNOWN_DESKTOP error) and pane (left/right/top/bottom — the window lands in its own split pane; an empty desktop absorbs the first window). New tools: ui-create-desktop (cap 10, optional name), ui-remove-desktop (windows migrate to the previous desktop, never the last one), ui-set-navbar (collapse/expand/toggle), ui-set-theme (dark/light/toggle). Four new ui.command kinds: create-desktop, remove-desktop, set-navbar-collapsed, set-theme — all frontend actions (target 'active').

Initial release (spec 20261022_ui-state-mca.md, REQ-5) — ui-state reads the user's live desktop per device (windows, layout, focus, dynamic window-type catalog, enriched names); ui-open / ui-close / ui-update-props broadcast window changes to all devices; ui-focus / ui-set-desktop are frontend actions on the active device. Thin wrapper over the backend ui.* domain via the admin_request bridge.
